WDED, History

The history of Star Wars by George Lucas spans several decades. It began with the first film, Star Wars, released on May 25, 1977. This was followed by two sequels: The Empire Strikes Back (1980) and Return of the Jedi (1983). These three films constitute the original trilogy.

Following a period of inactivity, the franchise was revived with a prequel trilogy starting in 1999 with The Phantom Menace, followed by Attack of the Clones (2002) and Revenge of the Sith (2005). An animated series, Star Wars: The Clone Wars, was released between 2008 and 2014, bridging the gap between the prequel and original trilogies.

In 2012, Lucasfilm was sold to The Walt Disney Company, leading to a sequel trilogy: The Force Awakens (2015), The Last Jedi (2017), and The Rise of Skywalker (2019). The franchise has also expanded into television with series like The Mandalorian and various spin-off films.

Expanded Universe

Prior to April 25, 2014, much of the expanded universe was considered non-canonical. On that date, Lucasfilm announced that the Expanded Universe (EU) would be rebranded as Star Wars Legends and that future stories would be told under the new canon label. Stories told under the Star Wars Legends label are non-canonical. The change was made to give "more freedom and flexibility to tell new stories" while preserving the continuity of the core films, animated series, and other projects.

Cultural Impact

Star Wars has had a profound impact on popular culture. The phrase "May the Force be with you" has become an iconic catchphrase. The franchise has influenced countless other works of fiction, inspired generations of fans, and created a multi-billion dollar industry encompassing films, television, merchandise, theme parks, and more.
